summary:
AgroVago is a smart agriculture platform developed by Team Vagodonera to help farmers choose crop rotations based on the environmental conditions and crop history of their fields. Our prototype focuses on Iowa, USA.
Farmers select and outline their fields on an interactive map. AgroVago combines NASA POWER climate records, SMAP soil moisture data, GPM IMERG precipitation, USDA SSURGO soil properties, USDA Cropland Data Layer crop history, and NOAA climate outlooks. Its simulation engine evaluates crop water requirements and historical climate scenarios, then compares five-year rotation alternatives according to agricultural constraints, diversification, and simulated water stress. Results include potential benefits, risks, and data limitations.
AgroVago aims to reduce uncertainty, improve water management, protect soil health, and support more informed, sustainable farming decisions. We hope to make scientific information accessible to farmers and expand the platform to additional agricultural regions.
We developed the prototype using TypeScript, React, Node.js, Vite, SQLite, Leaflet, and Excel, alongside NASA, USDA, and NOAA data services. We are integrating a Gemini-powered assistant to explain the platform’s results in plain language.
details:
AI Usage Disclosure

ChatGPT and OpenAI Codex were used for research, project planning, software development, debugging, and documentation. Google Gemini and Flow/Veo were used to generate visual content for the project presentation. AgroVago's agricultural simulations and crop rotation evaluations are calculated by its own scientific engine using NASA, USDA, and NOAA data. AI is used to support development, communication, and the explanation of scientific results, not to replace verified data or scientific calculations.
